reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Poisson.Compensated.MarkStep.Adapted -- reading (locked before any Lean)

Paper notion: the predictability (adaptedness) condition of an elementary compensated-Poisson
integrand: the coefficient of the step on (t_i,t_{i+1}] x B is F_{t_i}-measurable (sec. 3: H^2_N
consists of predictable integrands; elementary predictable integrands have coefficients
measurable at the left endpoint). Faithful Lean: a Prop stating that the coefficient(s) are
measurable w.r.t. F_{left endpoint} of the given filtration (the filtration w.r.t. which the
integral is formed, e.g. the driver's filtration), for each step. Not faithful: measurability at
the right endpoint or only ambient measurability.

Paper context (sec. 2, sec. 3, sec. 4, App. A). Standing basis: (Omega,F,(F_t),P) satisfying the usual
conditions, horizon T>0, d-dimensional Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random
measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E,E);
(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial
sigma-field F_0. Stochastic integrals int Z dW (Z in H^2_W: R^{m x d}-valued predictable,
E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 dt < oo) and int int U dNtilde (U in H^2_N) are the L^2 (Ito /
compensated-Poisson isometry) integrals; they are true L^2 martingales, cadlag, and are used in
identities holding a.s. for every t (sec. 3, "solution"). The paper never constructs these
integrals itself: it takes the standard construction (Applebaum sec. 4, He-Wang-Yan). So every
unit below is infrastructure: the paper's notion is the textbook one, and a faithful Lean
definition is one that (together with the other definitions) yields the textbook object on the
paper's basis for every integrand the paper's claims use; junk values outside that class are
harmless only if every proposition restricts to the class.

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Poisson.Compensated.MarkStep.Adapted (Poisson/MarkStepIsometry.lean:107-111)

Reading: a Prop stating the coefficient of each step is measurable for F at the LEFT endpoint of
its piece, for the filtration of the integral; not right endpoint, not ambient only.
Lean: Adapted F G := forall i < g.N0, forall k, StronglyMeasurable[F (g.p i)] (G.xi i k): the
coefficient of piece (p_i, p_{i+1}] and mark k is F_{p_i}-measurable (left endpoint); F is a
parameter (the docstring says "natural filtration" but the definition is for any filtration;
harmless docstring wording). Strong measurability of a real-valued function equals measurability.
Coefficients with i >= N0 are unconstrained, and they are unused. Matches.
Verdict: faithful.

author_review.disagreements:
No disagreement with the verdict. Wording note: the docstring says "adaptedness ... to the natural
filtration", while the definition is for an arbitrary filtration parameter F; the definition, not
the docstring, is what both reviews accept.
